findings.text: §7 sends the JT-60SA stamp through resolve_geometry_source "rather than a second resolver, so the stamp and the spine read one geometry route", but the stamp's sources (TransformGeometrySource.table_for at :320/:325, IdentityBoundCampaignGeometrySource, CampaignGeometrySource) read geometry via imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py read_geometry_table, whereas the spine's description comes from gs/artifact_resolution.py resolve_machine_description (imported and called at gs/machine_selection.py:130) — a machine-keyed frozen shot set added to resolve_geometry_source does not unify the two, so the map-under-test and the reference geometry the spine is scored against can diverge without any assertion catching it

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new module hides substantial behaviour behind one driving interface: tokamap_export (one exporter function over the catalogue and signal maps), eddb_remote.RemoteEddbExtractor.fetch_batch plus eddb.fetch_channels/write_channel over raw EDDB bytes, selene_deck.write_phase_description over three deck grammars and five IDSs, and the §7 EQDB reader riding the §3 transport. The per-IDS build_* helpers, transport/record DTOs and presence predicates are internal to that depth rather than parallel public entry points.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 asserts the benchmark stamp and the spine "read one geometry route", but the benchmark's geometry sources read through description_reader.read_geometry_table while the spine reads its machine description through gs/artifact_resolution.resolve_machine_description (nova's pinned artifact), so a JT-60SA machine key added to each keeps two owners for one machine description.
rubric_items.interface_budget: public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; pass — every section that adds surface states what it retires or why nothing can be: §2 "it retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter", §3 adds no `ambix data` command and "retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today", §4 "widens one protocol method and retires nothing" and its store-addressing keys "retire nothing", §6 generalises the entry point "rather than writing a second scorer", §7 "retires nothing, because no equilibrium-database reader exists in ambix".
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched both named codebases and cites by symbol the mechanisms it extends rather than rebuilds, and the citations resolve in code: description_reader.read_geometry_table, virtual_zarr.VirtualZarrView, cocos_convention.score_convention/score_conventions, challenge.convention._integrated_current, challenge.loader.load_shot/ChallengeShot, eval.efit_referee.judge_geometry/GeometryVerdict, spine_bench.runner._magnetics_residual, machine_map.MachineMapCatalog.flux_loop_positions_for and DescriptionSupplement, gs.artifact_resolution, gs.machine_selection, gs.machine_identity, spine_bench.transform_geometry_source, plus imas-codex's remote/EDAS layer.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every thin layer names in its own text why the underlying machinery cannot be extended: the §3 extractor owns its script rather than importing imas-codex (dependency direction), the cache shares paths.py and the zarr layout but takes none of the manifest/download CLI machinery, and the §7 EQDB reader uses the §3 transport and cache rather than a second path.
